components.note: Measurable parameter space, prior, sigma-finite dominating measure, jointly measurable normalized likelihood, P_theta, likelihood function, m, G, joint law Q, and the fixed-versus-random parameter distinction.

Normalization, mu(G)=1, the kernel version including the off-G convention, full disintegration via pi-lambda, absolute continuity and the integral formula for nonnegative and signed h; proved. Body 80-87 limits the exceptional-point reading.
Conditional-prior averaged densities and B_H defined for 0<Pi(H)<1, distinguished from maximized likelihoods.

Posterior probability and odds identity, increase iff B_H>1, every vanishing branch, and prior-null events; proved. Matches Kass-Raftery sec. 3.1 (posterior odds = Bayes factor x prior odds, held txt lines 255-300); sec. 6.1 locator also checked.

source_locators.locator: sec. 3.1 Definition (txt lines 255-300): posterior odds = Bayes factor x prior odds
sec. 6.1 Basic Ideas (txt lines 813-840): posterior model probabilities, eq. (16)

components.note: 11/122, 363/400, the duplicated report staying at 11/122, the general-p formula and its range 1/102 to 1/2, and the stipulated-model disclaimer; arithmetic rechecked; proof written.
History-dependent conditional densities, L_n, m_n, the regular path and Pi_i are defined.

Predictive factors r_i=m_i/m_{i-1}, successive updating equals batch, product and log identities, almost-sure regularity, order invariance in the exchangeable case, and failure of unconditional marginals (copied flag); proved.
Future kernel R(theta,x,.) with the conditional-independence special case and the predictive law are defined.
Predictive kernel property and conditional-law identity, mean and total-variance decomposition with integrability, and predictive covariance; proved.
Beta conjugacy including n=0, word versus count predictive, the beta-binomial future law with mean and variance, the worked beta(9,3) example and 15/26 versus 9/16; all rechecked and proved.

Posterior normal(u,v), the full marginal density with its constants, the one-observation and average future laws, covariance v, and the worked normal(1,1/2) and normal(1,9/2); the proof completes the square with constants retained.
Pushforward posterior, invariance under a transported bimeasurable reparameterization, and the theta versus eta=theta^2 uniform-prior example (2/3, 3/4; 1/2, 3/5); proved.
Reweighted posterior and evidence ratio, sharp bounds with attaining weights, the contamination mixture formula and a counterexample showing small contamination need not stay small; proved.
Product-measurable set procedure, posterior content almost everywhere, the coverage function, and the confidence guarantee distinguished.
Prior-average calibration identity, the one-Bernoulli 0.95 equal-tail counterexample with zero coverage at 0.99, and the normal credible interval content; proved.
Finite action set, bounded measurable loss, posterior risk, tie-resolved measurable Bayes action, and the loss as an explicit input.
Integrated-risk optimality, the expected-value-of-observation inequality, the two-action threshold with the worked change (1/21 versus 11/122), and the squared-error posterior mean; proved.
Expected log loss with its infinite branch, the Gibbs inequality with equality iff q=p, cumulative score -log m_n, and the scope disclaimer; proved.

A parameter-free recording factor cancels while a parameter-dependent one does not (2/3, 1/3 example), randomized stopping structure, first-success beta(alpha+1, beta+n-1), the count factor n, and selected-only versus predesignated trial; proved.
The procedure states inputs, record type, normalizer check, posterior and prediction, reporting, sensitivity, and the conditions requiring a changed model.
